acceptance: Each of SSB, TPC-DI and the read/write/transaction primitives has a recorded decision: relaxed (with generator validation at the new scales) or kept (docs updated).
docs/benchmarks/ssb.md and docs/benchmarks/tpc-di.md agree with the registry.
context: Found 2026-10-13 while reviewing why SSB, TPC-DI and primitives were not run at sf100 in the Snowflake trial-exit program.
description:
## Problem
`validate_scale_factor` (`benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.py:386-393`, commit 8c1589c4b, #332) rejects any scale not listed in `benchbox/core/benchmark_registry.yaml`. Current lists:
- TPC-DI and SSB: 0.01, 0.1, 1, 10 (lines 177-181 and 199-203)
- Read primitives: 0.01, 0.1 (282-284)
- Write and transaction primitives: 0.01, 0.1, 1 (303-306, 344-347)

The docs disagree. `docs/benchmarks/ssb.md:500` presents SSB sf100 as large-scale testing, and `docs/benchmarks/tpc-di.md:403-407` lists TPC-DI at 30 and above. `tests/unit/core/test_scale_factor_validation.py` covers only joinorder, TPC-H and ClickBench.

The lists look like scale menus that became hard limits as a side effect. They blocked SSB, TPC-DI and primitives runs at sf100 on Snowflake.

## Change
Decide per benchmark. Either relax the cap and validate the generator at the new scales, or keep it and state it in the docs. Pin the decision with tests.
